article.title: Why a Customer Can Move Down a Rank Without Spending Less
article.why: Separate absolute growth from relative position.

paragraphs.en:
Customer ranks are often built from relative measures such as percentiles, deciles, or quartiles. This creates an important interpretation problem: a customer can spend more money than last year and still move to a lower rank. The reason is simple. Rank depends not only on what one customer does, but also on what everyone else does.

Suppose a customer spent 150,000 yen last year and 160,000 yen this year. In absolute terms, spending increased by 10,000 yen, or about 6.7 percent. That sounds positive. However, imagine that many other customers increased their spending by 15 or 20 percent. The customer may then fall from the top 20 percent to the top 30 percent even though their own spending rose.

The reverse can also happen. A customer may spend slightly less but move upward if the rest of the population declines more sharply. This is why statements such as ‘customers in this segment improved’ can be misleading when improvement is defined only by rank movement. Rank tells us about relative position, not necessarily about absolute behavior.

For year-over-year analysis, it is therefore useful to show both measures. First, calculate the change in actual spending, transaction frequency, or another business metric. Second, calculate movement between rank bands. A transition matrix can show how many customers moved from D4 to D3, stayed in D4, or fell to D5. The actual-value change then tells us whether that movement reflects real growth, population-wide change, or both.

There is another complication: the population itself may change. New customers can enter, inactive customers can disappear, and eligibility rules can change. If the ranking base is different between years, the threshold for each rank can move even when customer behavior is stable. Analysts should therefore document the population definition and, when useful, run a common-customer analysis using only customers observed in both periods.

For business decisions, this distinction matters. If the goal is to encourage customers to reach a higher membership tier, management needs to know both the distance to the next threshold and whether the customer’s underlying spending is growing. A customer who is spending more but losing relative rank may still be a promising target. Conversely, a customer who moved up only because others declined may not have become more engaged.

A clear report might say: ‘The customer moved from D2 to D3, but annual spending increased by 6.7 percent. The decline is relative, not absolute.’ That one sentence prevents a common misunderstanding. Rank is useful, but it becomes much more informative when paired with the actual value behind it.
paragraphs.zh:
顧客排名常使用百分位、十分位或四分位等相對指標，因此會出現一個重要的解讀問題：顧客即使比去年花更多錢，排名仍可能下降。原因很簡單，排名不只取決於自己，也取決於其他所有人。

例如某顧客去年消費15萬日圓，今年16萬日圓，絕對金額增加1萬、約6.7%。但若其他顧客普遍成長15%或20%，他仍可能從前20%掉到前30%。反過來也可能發生：本人消費略降，但其他人降得更多，相對排名反而上升。

因此，以年度比較時最好同時呈現兩種尺度：實際消費額、次數等絕對變化，以及 rank band 的相對移動。transition matrix 可顯示 D4 到 D3、留在 D4 或掉到 D5 的人數，而實額變化則幫助判斷這是實際成長、整體母體變動，還是兩者共同造成。

另一個問題是母體本身會改變。新客加入、休眠客消失、資格條件變動，都可能使各 rank 的門檻改變。因此應記錄母體定義，必要時另外做只包含兩期皆存在顧客的 common-customer analysis。

在商業決策上這個區別很重要。若目標是促進會員升級，就需要同時知道距離下一門檻還有多少，以及底層消費是否正在成長。消費增加但相對排名下降的人仍可能是有潛力的對象；只因其他人衰退而升級的人則未必真的提高 engagement。

清楚的報告可以寫成：「該顧客由 D2 降至 D3，但年度消費額增加6.7%，這是相對下降而非絕對下降。」Rank 很有用，但搭配背後實際數值才更有解釋力。
paragraphs.ja:
顧客rankはpercentile、decile、quartileなどの相対指標で作られることが多いため、本人の利用額が増えてもrankが下がることがあります。rankは本人だけでなく、他の顧客の動きにも左右されるからです。

例えば前年15万円、今年16万円なら、絶対額では1万円、約6.7％増えています。しかし他顧客が15～20％伸びれば、上位20％から上位30％へ下がる可能性があります。逆に本人の利用額が少し減っても、全体がそれ以上に落ちれば相対順位は上がります。

前年比較では、実利用額や利用回数などの絶対変化とrank帯の相対移動を併記すると有効です。transition matrixでD4からD3への上昇、D4維持、D5への下降を示し、実額変化でそれが実成長なのか母集団全体の変化なのかを確認します。

さらに母集団自体も変化します。新規顧客の流入、休眠顧客の離脱、eligibility条件の変更によってrank thresholdが動くことがあります。そのため母集団定義を記録し、必要なら両年に存在する共通顧客だけでも分析します。

会員rank-up施策では、次rankまでの距離と基礎的な利用額の伸びを両方見る必要があります。利用額が伸びながら相対rankが下がった顧客は依然有望かもしれません。一方、他者の低下だけでrank-upした顧客はengagementが高まったとは限りません。

「D2からD3へ下がりましたが、年間利用額は6.7％増加しており、絶対的な減少ではなく相対順位の低下です」と説明すれば誤解を防げます。rankは実額と組み合わせることで、より有用な指標になります。

vocabulary.usage: The rank is based on percentiles.
The threshold can move each year.
A higher rank does not always mean more engaged.

business.term: The decline is relative, not absolute.

business.explanation: 建議報告同時呈現兩個尺度。
